oneLiner: The quantum pure-play with actual revenue: 287% growth, a $2B war chest and a foundry roll-up, priced at roughly 55x sales in a sector that has already halved once on a single comment.
thesis: Hypergrowth with receipts. Q2 2026 revenue of $80.1M grew 287% YoY, beat consensus by roughly 20%, and marked the fifth consecutive record quarter after Q1 2026 grew 755%. Full-year guidance has been raised twice in 2026, from $225-245M in February to $280-290M in August.

A war chest no pure-play peer can match. Cash, equivalents and investments were $3.0B at June 30, 2026, roughly $2.0B pro forma after the $1.8B SkyWater close on July 31 - the residue of $3.0B in Heights Capital-led raises in July and October 2025. IonQ can outspend QBTS, RGTI and the newly listed entrants combined.

The technical roadmap keeps arriving early. AQ64 was reached on the Tempo system in September 2025, three months ahead of plan, with 99.99% two-qubit fidelity; management says it has made major strides toward a 256-qubit machine in 2026 and has published error-correction results on its own hardware.

Vertical integration is a genuine strategy shift. Oxford Ionics ($1.075B, closed September 2025), SkyWater Technology ($1.8B, closed July 2026) and Nexus Photonics give IonQ chip design, integrated photonics and a US foundry - a full-stack merchant-supplier position in the allied quantum ecosystem.

Backlog underwrites the guide. Remaining performance obligations hit $470M in Q1 2026, up 554% YoY, and the mix is broadening: roughly 60% of Q2 2026 revenue was commercial enterprise, about 50% international, and about 25% came from multi-product customers.

latestProse: Q2 2026, reported August 5: revenue of $80.1M grew 287% YoY, beat consensus by roughly 20%, and made a fifth consecutive record quarter. The headline GAAP net loss of $1.87B is mostly optics - about $1.6B was non-cash mark-to-market on the Heights Capital warrants - but the operating reality is still heavy: adjusted EBITDA loss of $120.3M, or $95.6M excluding SkyWater-related commercial costs. Cash stood at $3.0B at June 30, roughly $2.0B pro forma after the $1.8B SkyWater close on July 31. Mix improved: about 50% international, 60% commercial enterprise, 25% multi-product. Standalone FY26 guidance rose to $280-290M with roughly 100% organic growth claimed. The disclosure that matters most: adjusted EBITDA burn is now annualizing near $480M, so the $2.0B war chest funds about four years unless gross profit scales materially faster.
guidanceProse: FY26 guidance went to $280-290M standalone, the second raise this year (February: $225-245M; May: $260-270M), with management claiming roughly 100% organic growth and explicitly excluding SkyWater, which consolidates from Q3. The central debate is revenue quality: how much is durable QCaaS and networking versus lumpy government and national-lab system deals, and how much growth was effectively purchased through acquisitions. Bulls point to $470M of remaining performance obligations (Q1 2026, +554% YoY) as the bridge; bears note the guide implies second-half deceleration from Q2's $80M run rate.
segments: Quantum computing: Forte/Tempo system sales plus QCaaS through the major clouds - about 25% of Q2 2026 revenue came from multi-product customers.
Quantum networking and security: ID Quantique, Qubitekk and now Nexus Photonics chip-scale lasers and optical subsystems aimed at data-center-scale quantum networking.
Foundry (consolidates from Q3 2026): SkyWater Technology, a US pure-play chip foundry (roughly $300M-plus historical annual revenue, unverified), positioned as a quantum photonics foundry offering.
competitive: D-Wave (QBTS): $3.1M Q2 2026 revenue, annealing-first with a new gate-model program - 26x smaller than IonQ by quarterly revenue yet valued at about $7.7B.

Rigetti (RGTI): $5.1M Q2 2026 revenue, $28.1M operating loss; superconducting gate-model; signed an LOI with the US Department of Commerce for up to $100M in exchange for a non-controlling equity stake.
IBM: the gate-model scale benchmark, targeting the fault-tolerant Starling system for 2029; IonQ's September 2025 AQ64 claim was explicitly benchmarked against IBM machines.

The public comp set exploded in 2026: IQM (26 systems sold, 17 delivered, EUR 102M backlog) listed in July, Quantinuum and Infleqtion reported debut results in August, and Google opened early access to its 105-qubit Willow chip in March 2026.
moat: IonQ has the deepest balance sheet and broadest commercial traction among quantum pure-plays, plus differentiated trapped-ion fidelity (99.99% two-qubit) and now its own foundry. But nobody, IonQ included, has demonstrated commercially valuable quantum advantage; today's revenue is early-adopter systems, cloud access and networking gear, not proven end-market pull. The moat is capital, roadmap velocity and vertical integration - not a defensible installed base.
risks: The multiple prices in flawless execution. Roughly 55x EV to standalone FY26 guidance leaves no room for a slipped government deal or missed milestone, in a sector that halved in a day on Jensen Huang's January 2025 comments.

Dilution is structural. The two Heights Capital deals (July and October 2025) sold about 39M shares plus roughly 79M warrants, many struck at $99.88; the $1.6B Q2 2026 warrant remeasurement loss shows the size of the overhang, and it grows with every rally.

The roll-up is untested. Six-plus acquisitions since 2024 (Oxford Ionics, SkyWater, Nexus Photonics, Vector Atomic, ID Quantique and others) must be integrated simultaneously; SkyWater is a low-margin foundry that transforms the income statement and could blur the growth story.
Burn is accelerating with ambition. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $120.3M in Q2 2026 alone, annualizing near $480M, versus $95.6M excluding SkyWater costs - spending is scaling faster than gross profit.

Revenue quality is debatable. Growth leans on lumpy system deals with governments and national labs, and skeptics argue part of the organic-growth claim was purchased via acquisitions; the standalone guide implies H2 deceleration from Q2's run rate.

Trapped ions may not win. IBM (fault-tolerant Starling targeted for 2029), Google (Willow early access, March 2026) and superconducting and neutral-atom rivals scale qubit counts faster; if ion gate-speed limits bind before error-corrected utility arrives, the roadmap premium evaporates.
catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings, early November 2026 - first quarter consolidating SkyWater.
256-qubit system demonstration targeted by end-2026 on the Oxford Ionics EQC roadmap.
Quantum photonics foundry product announcements with SkyWater and Nexus Photonics, H2 2026.
US Department of Commerce $2B quantum program awards finalize through H2 2026 (IonQ participation unverified).
Peer prints: Quantinuum (Aug 11) and Infleqtion (Aug 12) debut public reports reset sector comps.
pricedIn: At $43.44 (August 11, 2026) IonQ's market cap is around $17.6B (sources quote $14.9-17.6B on differing share counts), or roughly $15.6B EV net of about $2.0B pro forma cash. That is about 55x the $285M midpoint of standalone FY26 guidance - and the stock still sits 59% below its 52-week high near $106. The price implies quantum computing becomes a real multi-billion-dollar product category this decade with IonQ as the vertically integrated western champion. The key debate: whether 287% growth against $470M of RPO justifies a 50x-plus sales multiple, or whether this is the fastest-growing line item inside a hype cycle that has already halved once.

scenarios.bear: A quantum-winter narrative returns: a high-profile technical disappointment or government budget slippage stalls bookings, FY27 growth decelerates below 50%, and SkyWater's low-margin foundry revenue muddies the story. The roughly 79M outstanding Heights warrants cap every rally while adjusted EBITDA burn runs near $500M a year. The multiple compresses from about 55x toward 10-15x sales and the stock revisits the mid-teens, with cash runway becoming the dominant question.
scenarios.base: FY26 lands inside the $280-290M standalone guide and 2027 grows 60-80% on Tempo deployments, networking revenue and a first full year of SkyWater consolidation. Burn stays heavy but the $2.0B balance sheet absorbs it without emergency issuance beyond warrant exercises. The multiple compresses gradually as revenue grows into it; the stock chops in a wide $35-65 band, tracking quantum sentiment, RPO prints and the 256-qubit milestone timeline.
scenarios.bull: The 256-qubit demonstration lands by end-2026 with error-correction results that convert into data-center-scale orders through 2027. SkyWater makes IonQ the merchant foundry for the allied quantum ecosystem, revenue tracks toward $1B by 2028 with gross margins holding above 50%, and warrant exercises at $99.88 become a funding source rather than an overhang. The stock takes out its roughly $106 high on the combination of growth and scarcity value.

valPresets.note: Deeply unprofitable ($120.3M adjusted EBITDA loss in Q2 2026 alone), so revenue mode with a horizon FCF margin and exit multiple is the only defensible frame. Presets compound the $285M FY26 standalone guide midpoint; at roughly 55x EV/sales the base case (40% CAGR for 8 years to about $4B revenue) lands near today's EV - the market already pays for the base case, so the equity argument rests on the bull path.
